question: The All-India Services Act, 1951, allows which authority to frame rules for All-India service recruitment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The All-India Services Act, 1951, empowers the **Central Government** to frame rules and regulations for the recruitment and conditions of service of All-India Services such as IAS, IPS, and IFS.
 
• This authority is derived under Article 312 of the Indian Constitution, which allows Parliament to create All-India Services common to both the Union and States.
 
• The Central Government ensures uniformity in service conditions and recruitment processes across states for these services.
 
• Rules framed by the Central Government under this Act are known as the All-India Services Rules, which cover aspects like recruitment, promotion, and disciplinary actions.
 
• The Act aims to maintain efficiency, integrity, and coordination in administrative services across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All-India Services:**

 
 
• These services include the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Forest Service (IFS).
 
• Officers in these services serve both the Central Government and State Governments.
 
• They are recruited through the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and governed by rules framed under the All-India Services Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Role of UPSC:**
 
 
• The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts exams like Civil Services Examination for recruitment into All-India Services.
 
• It acts as an advisory body on recruitment rules framed by the Central Government.
 
 
 
• **Article 312 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• It allows Parliament to create All-India Services if deemed necessary in the national interest.
 
• Such services are considered vital for maintaining administrative uniformity and efficiency across the country.
 
 
 
• **Central Government’s Role:**
 
 
• It frames and implements service rules to ensure uniformity and coordination among states.
 
• Decisions related to pay scales, promotions, and disciplinary actions are governed centrally.
